summary: Keiichi Miyamoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1966 to 1997 under Minoru Hara. He was a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (1975) and taught at Kokugakuin University (1986–1995).

Keiji Iwata specialized in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1941 to 1944. He later held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (circa 1973–1976) and Otani University (circa 1986–1993).

Keiji Nishitani was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Hajime Tanabe, and at the University of Freiburg under Martin Heidegger, he held long-term posts at Otani University and Kyoto University.

Keiki Yabuki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Jōdo Shū Tōhoku Shikō, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. His career included posts at Shukyo University (circa 1913–1926), University of Tokyo, and Taisho University (circa 1926–1939).

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Academic appointments include serving as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies (attested 2015).

Keir Strickland works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham and studied at the University of the Highlands and Islands, later working at the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University.
Keishi Renja works in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University in the doctoral program (attested 2013), where he also held a post as a research student.

Keishin Okamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Kyoto University between 1949 and 1959. He held academic appointments at Koyasan University (1959–1973, 2005–2009) and Kochi University (circa 1970–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Tohoku University. He held professorial posts at Rissho University and Tohoku University, and later served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (circa 1992–2002).

Keith Dowman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under numerous traditional teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Kangyur Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (circa 1978–1984) and held teaching and administrative posts at Shuchiin University (attested 1995–2005) and Taisho University (attested 1995–2017).

Keizaburo Mizuno is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He worked at Tokyo National Museum, Tokyo University of the Arts, Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art, and the Hanzomon Museum.

Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery and other monasteries under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977 and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018) and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science.
Kemu Jin was an Indologist, Sinologist, and linguist. He served on the faculty at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became a Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

Ken McLeod is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the University of British Columbia and trained under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa. He was resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (circa 1985–1990).
Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and earned his PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

Kengo Harimoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999. He held posts at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo between circa 1973 and 1983, and he held an academic post at Kokugakuin University from circa 1990 to 2020.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1972 to 1980 and under Seizan Yanagida from circa 1976 to 1984.
